To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sample size of interviews is not justified in most of the IS qualitative studies in this dataset, and that the number of interviews is correlated with cultural variables, such as the journal of publication, the number of authors, and the world region.

(1) IS qualitative studies are often not rigorous in their justification of sample size; (2) the number of interviews in IS qualitative studies is often correlated with cultural factors (journal of publication, number and type of authors, world regions), suggesting the subjective nature of the number of interviews; and (3) the optimal ranges of interviews in IS studies are: 10-20 for case study, 20-30 for ethnographic, 30-50 for grounded theory, and
the sample size of interviews is correlated with cultural factor and there are no optimal ranges of interviews in qualitative research.

the question of whether sample size in qualitative studies matters. Our research suggests that it does matter, at least to some extent.
